payload.friendly_name: ASN.1 Tree Delete, Copy and Paste
payload.purpose_context: crex users editing BER/DER structures can currently only delete or insert one element at a time in the ASN.1 tree. This mission adds Shift+Up/Down marking of multiple elements, deletion of the marked range, and copy/paste of whole ASN.1 subtrees so restructuring documents becomes fast and keyboard-driven.
payload.purpose_tldr: Let users mark, delete, copy and paste ASN.1 elements in the tree pane with keyboard shortcuts.

options: Contiguous siblings under one parent only
Any contiguous run of visible rows regardless of depth
payload.question: When the user holds Shift and presses Up/Down in the ASN.1 tree, what may the marked range span?

payload.final_answer: Contiguous siblings under one parent only; a marked constructed element implicitly includes its whole subtree

options: Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V via system clipboard as DER hex, plus in-app buffer
y/p vim-style with in-app buffer only
payload.question: Which keys trigger copy/paste in the tree and where does copied data live (in-app buffer vs system clipboard)?

payload.final_answer: Both paths (y/p in-app and Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V system clipboard), selected by a configuration option toggling between 'normal' (Ctrl+C/V) and 'vim' key bindings. Configuration persisted in the OS-typical user config location. The setting also governs the content editor: with vim bindings it gets a vim-style insert mode entered with 'i' etc. A new File top-bar menu entry opens a config editor (initially only the key-binding choice).

options: Modal core: normal/insert modes, hjkl/0/$ motion, x, v visual selection, y/d/p, u undo
Insert-mode toggle only: i enters typing, Esc leaves it, everything else unchanged
payload.question: With vim key bindings configured, how much of vim's modal editing do the value editors (hex, text, integer, OID ...) adopt?

payload.final_answer: Modal core (normal/insert modes, i/a/I/A, Esc, h/j/k/l/0/$, x, v visual, y/d/p, u). In vim bindings Ctrl+C/X/V/Z do NOT act as in normal bindings; Ctrl+A increments and Ctrl+X decrements the number under the cursor as in vim. The vim key-binding space must stay free of normal-mode artifacts so more vim functions can be added later.

options: Std-only: env-var based OS paths and a hand-written key = value parser (TOML-compatible subset)
payload.question: How should the settings file be located and parsed: with new crates (dirs + toml/serde) or with a zero-dependency std-only implementation?

payload.final_answer: Std-only: env-var based OS paths and a hand-written key = "value" parser (TOML-compatible subset), no new crates

payload.question: Is the Engineering Alignment (keymap translation layer, new modules keymap/settings/vim, element buffer as DER bytes, vim modes as editor wrapper) confirmed?

payload.wp_title: Clipboard paste-source reading with PEM support
Element buffer, delete/cut/copy/yank of the operand
Edit menu, File ▸ Settings entry and dialogs
